case_name: Kumari Shikha vs Lalkrishna Dutta Thakur
facts_of_case: Appellant sought declaration under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. No solemnization date mentioned in application.

legal_principles.principle: A Family Court shall have and exercise all the jurisdiction exercisable by any district court or any subordinate civil Court under any law for the time being in force.
legal_principles.held: It reads thus: A Family Court shall - (a) have and exercise all the jurisdiction exercisable by any district court or any subordinate civil Court under any law for the time being in force.

legal_principles.principle: A Family Court shall also have and exercise the jurisdiction exercisable by a Magistrate of the first class under Chapter IX of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
legal_principles.held: Subject to the other provisions of this Act, a Family Court shall also have and exercise - (a) the jurisdiction exercisable by a Magistrate of the first class under Chapter IX relating to order for maintenance of wife, children and parents) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Chapter IX

outcome.final_order: Ultimate order of dismissal of application under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 cannot be faulted.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nullum tempus occurrit regi
use_for_drafting: drafting petition for nullity of marriage
